page0.text:
After we finish eating dinner, I receive a call from Tohsaka.
Regarding the incident at school, It seems like there are a lot fewer victims than we had thought.
It must be because Rider, the Servant who set up the Bounded Field, was defeated quickly.

page1.text:
From what I understand, the students that were in the same classroom as Rider need to stay longer in the hospital, but most of them just have anemia.
School's not going to close down, and we'll be having classes like usual tomorrow."

page2.text:
"Shirou, what did Rin say?"
"She says that school's going on like normal. So we'll go tomorrow and look for Caster's Master."

page3.text:
"...I see. Then no one suffered any serious injuries?"
"There were a few. Oh, I think Fuji-nee's not home yet because she's busy with a staff meeting or something."

page4.text:
"That is good. I am sure she will be sitting at the dining table tomorrow morning as though nothing happened."
Yeah, I'm relieved too.
Well, she has extraordinary strength, so I wasn't worried once I heard that everyone was safe.

page5.text:
"...Then, Shirou. Continuing our conversation from earlier..."
Saber leans over the table with a serious expression.
"...Ugh. So you haven't given up yet, Saber?"

page6.text:
"Of course not. I will sleep in your room so that we do not repeat last night's mistake. You do not have any complaints, right?"
...
Of course I have complaints.
Having Saber sleep in my room is like telling me to die.

page7.text:
"Shirou. First of all, it is your fault for falling sway to long-distance hypnosis from such a great distance.
I cannot protect you from Caster's magecraft, so it is natural for me to at least stay in the same room."

page8.text:
"The closer I am, the better I can sense magecraft. If Caster is after you, I cannot sleep away from you."
"Well, that is a very sound argument, but, Saber..."
I don't think Caster would use the same strategy since she failed once already.

page9.text:
That's what I think, but if I were to say that to Saber right now...
"...You're too optimistic! That's why you were tricked by a fiend like Caster and insulted by someone with a twisted personality like Archer! It's because you are as overly agreeable as the chocolate bun we had for dessert!"
It'll be something like that.

page10.text:
"Are you listening, Shirou!? I will not let listen to these 'but you are a woman' excuses. I will be sleeping in your room starting tonight, so please do not escape to the shed in the middle of the night!"
Saber glares at me.

page11.text:
...Oof, she even anticipated that I was going to run away to the shed.
I'll have to hold out and try to get her to agree on a compromise.

page12.text:
"...All right. I'll have you sleep near me."
"So you finally accept it, huh? Yes, that is the obvious choice as a Master."

page13.text: "But not in the same room. You know there's an empty room next to mine, right? On the other side of the sliding door."

page14.text:
"Mm? Yes, I know, but what about it?"
"Um, that place should be good enough to protect me while I'm asleep, right? Well, first of all, the enemy won't even come in if we're sleeping in the same room.
If you are standing by in the next room over, then you can attack the enemy the moment they've let their guard down."
Oh, I feel like I'm making sense here.

page15.text: "That's enough right, Saber? To be honest, I don't know about two people sleeping in that small room. We physically can't fit. I think it's bad as Servant to cause her Master lack of sleep."

page16.text:
"Hm... You certainly found a silver tongue tonight, Shirou.
Understood. It still sounds like an excuse to me, but fine. I shall agree to that plan."

page17.text:
"...Phew."
Good.
Man, being a Master is hard enough.
If I sleep in the same room as Saber on top of that, my processor will overheat.

page18.text: With that, the chaotic day comes to an end.

page19.text:
It's becoming a habit to train with Saber until eleven and spend an hour doing my routine in the shed.
I get back to my room when the date changes and hear Saber's breathing as she sleeps.

page20.text:
...
I feel myself getting flustered from the thought and try to keep my cool as I get in bed.
I close my eyes, shaking away any thoughts, and tell myself to get to sleep as soon as possible.

page21.text:
"...As if I can sleep that fast, stupid."
I try my best not to think about Saber and look back at what happened today.
The red school.
A field of blood that would have created lots of victims had we not stopped it.

page22.text:
...
That blows any frivolous thoughts away.
The students collapsed in the red classroom.
She was desperately bearing the sight of Rider collapsed on the floor and the students that looked like corpses.

page23.text:
...Oh, I remember.
At that moment, I was able to find out a deep part of her.

page24.text:
I'll kill you the next time we meet.
I mean we're enemies, right?

page25.text:
Though she acts like a distinguished mage, she's never crossed the final line.
She's brave, strong, and has a charming regality about her, but she's also incredibly good-natured.

page26.text:
That difference must be her burden.
...The one area where she fumbles.
The more she tries to act like a mage, the more she denies herself.
